summary: Selective, visible enrichment is better grounded than indiscriminate context stuffing, provided block selection, provenance and outcome measurement are treated as product behavior rather than hidden prompt craft.

points.text: Long-context evidence makes a concrete case for a token report and selection step: merely fitting more blocks into the window does not ensure the model will use the relevant one.
Versioned blocks linked to traces make changes auditable and allow evaluation by block version, task class and outcome instead of relying on anecdotal prompt quality.
Showing the classifier decision, sources and inserted text gives the operator a chance to catch wrong routing, sensitive-data leakage and obsolete guidance before execution.
Retrieved or centrally curated content remains an instruction-injection surface; enrichment needs trust boundaries and instruction/data separation, not provenance labels alone.
